The present appeal has been instituted assailing the judgment dated 28-02-2014, passed by the learned Sessions Judge, Karimganj, in Sessions Case No. 17/2011 convicting the appellant, herein,
under Section 498 IPC and sentencing him to undergo rigorous imprisonment for 02 (two) years along with payment of fine of Rs. 5000/- (Rupees Five Thousand), in default to undergo rigorous imprisonment for another 03 (three) months.

3. The prosecution case, in brief, is that one Abdul Haque had lodged an FIR on 11- 01-2010, with the Officer-in-Charge, Karimganj Police Station, inter-alia, alleging therein that his wife Rejia Begum who used to reside at his native place along with one son and a daughter, while the informant was residing in Roing, Arunachal Pradesh, had fled away with the appellant, herein, along with 04 (four) month old minor daughter.
In the FIR, it was further stated that on being informed about the incident, the informant returned to his native place and made a search for his wife.

During the search, it was revealed that an amount of Rs. 60,000/- (Rupees Sixty Thousand) along with gold and silver ornaments were taken away by his wife and the appellant, herein, had also taken an amount of Rs. 1,15,000/- (Rupees One Lakh Fifteen Thousand) from his own house.

It was also disclosed that during the search it had come to light that Rejia Begum along with the appellant,
herein, and her minor daughter were staying at Jarkat, Aizawl, Mizoram.
The police on receipt of the FIR, registered the same as Karimganj P.S. Case No. 17/2010 under Section 366/ 380 IPC.
On conclusion of the investigation, the Investigating Officer submitted charge-sheet against the appellant under Section 366/ 376 IPC.

The case being committed to the court Page No.# 3/7 of learned Sessions Judge, Karimganj, charge under Section 366/ 376 IPC came to be framed against the appellant and the same being read over and explained to the appellant, herein, he having pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried, a trial ensued in the matter.

During the pendency of the trial and after recording the deposition of the 03 (three) prosecution witnesses, an application was moved by the learned P.P. for alteration of charge and accordingly, the learned Trial Court upon appreciating the materials on record, charge under Section 498 IPC was also framed against the appellant, herein, which was also explained to him and he had pleaded not guilty, the trial thereafter continued.

On conclusion of the trial, the learned Trial Court, upon examining the evidences coming on record,
proceeded vide judgment dated 28-02-2014 to convict the appellant, herein, under Section 498 IPC and sentenced him to imprisonment as noticed, hereinabove.
The appellant, being aggrieved has instituted the present proceeding.
4. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and also perused the materials available on record.
5. The allegation against the appellant, herein, is of having facilitated the moving away of the victim Rejia Begum wife of the informant from her matrimonial house.

The learned Trial Court, upon considering the evidences coming on record, had drawn the following conclusions:-

sentences.text: In the light of the above, evidence on the record is to be considered.

In Page No.#
4/7 the instant case there is no evidence by any eyewitness that at the time of leaving of the matrimonial house by the DW 1 accused was physically present there to take away.
So, plainly it can he said that the accused did not take away the wife of the complainant, the DW 1 from the house of the complainant.
But it reveals in the evidence that since after her leaving she has been residing with the accused.
According to the defence, the DW I was divorced by the complainant over telephone.

The DW 1 in her evidence stated that the accused used to visit her previous matrimonial house wherefrom being assaulted by her previous parents in law she came out with her baby daughter and informed the accused to extend her help.
At first the accused refused.
Hearing her condition the accused gave her shelter.
After that hearing about the same the complainant over telephone divorced her pronouncing 'talak'.
Then she got married with the accused.
Now, even if this piece of evidence is believed, then it can surely be said that after her leaving and staying with the accused the said talak was pronounced.
Therefore, it can be arrived at that till her leaving she was married wife of the accused which was well within the knowledge of the accused.

Moreover, this piece of evidence difficult to be relied upon mainly on the ground that she as wife of the accused adduced the evidence and that too, coming from the custody of the accused contradicting her previous statement recorded us.
164 Cr.PC. the Ext.5 that she had a prior physical relation with the accused.
11. Ld. counsel for the prosecution strongly contended that mother of the child is the best person to say about the paternity.
Here in the instant case the DW 1 in her previous statement, the Ext.5, stated that her female daughter was born as a result of her physical relation with the accused.
The same is however contradicted by the DW 1 stating that she under threat of her parents-in-laws and previous husband ie. the complainant gave the statement accordingly before the Magistrate.
This evidence is also not believable mainly on the aforesaid ground.

12. The DW 1 in her evidence deposed that that she at her own instance took shelter in the house of the accused and the accused did not induce her or entice her away,
rather on her repeated request gave her shelter. If actually shelter was so required she could have taken shelter at her parent's house instead of going with the accused to some unknown place.

Therefore, it clearly appears that she and the accused had nurtured an intention to get married with each other, and for fulfillment of the same the accused assisted her to get away from her husband's house and subsequently also extended his co-operation.

It further clearly appears that she left the house being influenced by the accused who used to visit her previous matrimonial house in the absence of the complainant and also disregarding the objection of the PW 5.
This piece of evidence of regular visit disregarding of the objection as come out in the evidence of PW 5 is not at all categorically denied in the cross examination.

13. The father of the accused, the PW 4 deposed that on the date of the alleged occurrence when he returned home came to know that Rejia Begum (DW Jashim Uddin vs State Of Assam And Anr on 3 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146119442/
3 1) fled away with his son, the accused and after that the accused did not return Page No.# 5/7 back to his home and he (PW 4) could not say till date the where-about of the accused.

sentences.text: This piece of evidence is not denied in the cross examination.
Even his evidence that the accused took away all transaction money kept in his shop is also not denied,

That being so, it is abundantly clear that both the accused and the DW I had a pre-plan to go away for fulfilling their lust and they concealed themselves for about 5 days till their recovery by police.
Therefore it can be arrived at that the accused with intent to had illicit relation concealed and detained the DW 1 in his custody.
Evidence of the DW 1 is found to be very shaky in consistent with regard to all the material facts.
She even failed to state her date of marriage with the accused.
It clearly appears that she only to save her husband, the accused adduced false evidence contradicting her previous statement in the Ext. 5 which supports the charge u/s. 498 IPC.
That apart all the aforesaid acts on the part of the accused thus clearly constitute the offence within the meaning of section 498 IPC.
The charges as framed u/s. 366/376 IPC is not attracted in this case mainly on the ground that the victim being a major went with the accused at her own will.

14. From the above discussion, contentions and deduction and consideration of the evidence in its entirety it is held that prosecution has been able to prove the charge u/s. 498 IPC beyond all reasonable doubt Therefore the accused is held guilty and convicted accordingly.

The other charges being not attracted and proved the accused is acquitted from the same as framed u/s. 366/376 IPC"
6. Having convicted the appellant, herein, in the above manner, the learned Trial Court sentenced him as follows:-
"15 Heard the accused on the question of sentence.
Having due regard to the above and considering the facts and circumstances of this case under which the offence was committed I find no ground to deal with the accused with leniency.

The accused is therefore convicted and sentenced u/s. 498 IPC with rigorous imprisonment (RI) of 2 (two) years and also with fine of Rs. 5,000/- (Rupees five thousand) and in default shall further undergo R.I. for a period of 3 (three) months."
7. This Court has perused the conclusions drawn by the learned Trial Court in the light of the evidences coming on record.
This Court notices that it is settled position of law that the provision of Section 498 IPC are intended to protect the rights of the husband and not those of the wife.

The evidences coming on record having demonstrated that the Page No.# 6/7 appellant, herein, had facilitated the leaving of her matrimonial house by the wife of the informant, the willingness of wife being immaterial, when the charge against the appellant is under Section 498 IPC, this Court in the light of the evidences coming on record is of the considered view that the conclusions drawn by the learned Trial Court were so drawn basing on due and proper examination of the evidences coming on record and no infirmity is found therein.
Accordingly, this Court is of the view that the conviction of the appellant under Section 498 IPC would not mandate any interference.

sentences.text: Having drawn the above conclusions, this Court finds that the offence was committed by the appellant, herein, on 07-01-2010 and around 15 years have lapsed since the date of commission of the offence by the appellant, herein.

Further from the evidences coming on record, this Court notices that the appellant and the wife of the informant, are presently living as husband and wife after having got married and further the informant had also performed second marriage and is living with his second wife and a daughter born out of the said wedlock.
The appellant, herein, is also found to having been litigating in the matter for the last around 15 years.
Accordingly, this Court is of the considered view that the sentencing of the appellant, herein, would mandate a modification.

9. The appellant, herein, having been convicted under Section 498 IPC, the provisions thereof being relevant, is extracted here-in-below:-
"Section 498 - Enticing or taking away or detaining with criminal intent a married woman- Whoever takes or entices away any woman who is and whom he knows or has reason to believe to be the wife of any other man, from that man, or from any person having the care of her on behalf of that man, with intent that she may have illicit intercourse with any person, or conceals or Page No.# 7/7 detains with that intent any such woman, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both."

A perusal of the provisions of Section 498 IPC mandates imposition of alternative punishment, i.e.
imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to 02 (two) years, or with fine, or with both, this Court for the reasons noticed hereinabove is of the considered view that ends of justice would met in the event the sentencing is modified to that of payment of fine of Rs. 5000/-
(Rupees Five Thousand).
10.

Accordingly, in view of the above discussions, this Court modifies the sentencing of the appellant, herein, by the learned Trial Court vide judgment dated 28-02-2014 and limits the same to the payment of fine of Rs. 5000/- (Rupees Five Thousand), in default to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a further period of 03 (three) months.

11. The appellant, herein, shall appear before the learned Trial Court within a period of 02 (two)
months from today to deposit the fine amount.
11. With the above observations and directions, this appeal stands disposed of.

12. Registry to send back the TCR along with a copy of this order for information and necessary action.
JUDGE
